reading.body:
Compute North was a Bitcoin mining hosting company headquartered in Minnesota that operated large-scale facilities in several states before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2022. This Nebraska site, tagged in OpenStreetMap as Compute North and reportedly built for cryptocurrency mining rather than conventional colocation, carries a published IT capacity of 30 MW. The facility's current operational status, whether it continues mining under a successor owner, remains idle, or has been decommissioned, could not be confirmed.

Nebraska has 21 mapped data center facilities but publishes no IT capacity figures from operator spec pages. This Compute North site, at 30 MW, ranks first among Nebraska facilities with a published capacity figure. The state context makes clear that most mapped facilities in Nebraska disclose no power figures, so this 30 MW represents an isolated data point rather than a measure of the state's total AI or hosting infrastructure.

At typical Bitcoin mining densities of roughly 10 to 15 kW per rack, 30 MW would support approximately 2,000 to 3,000 racks of mining hardware. This capacity is substantial for a single facility but cannot be counted as active AI compute until the site's post-bankruptcy status is confirmed and its current use is independently verified.
